en: Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Usamah informed me, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and from al-Nu'man ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of the hadith of Ya'qub.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Qari—narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, he said: I heard Sahl saying: I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "I am your forerunner at the Basin; whoever comes to it will drink, and whoever drinks will never thirst, ever. Groups of people whom I know and who know me will surely come to me, then a barrier will be placed between me and them." Abu Hazim said: Al-Nu'man ibn Abi 'Ayyash heard me while I was narrating this hadith to them, and said: "Is this how you heard Sahl speak?" He said: I said: "Yes." He said: "And I bear witness regarding Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that I heard him add to it, saying: 'Indeed, they are of me!' But it will be said: 'Indeed, you do not know what they did after you.' So I will say: 'Away! Away with whoever altered after me!'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Bishr narrated to us, all of them from Mis'ar; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, they said: Shu'bah narrated to us, both from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Jundab, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to me, Za'idah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr narrated to us, he said: I heard Jundab saying: I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "I am your forerunner at the Basin."

Muslim said: And it was narrated to me from Abu Usamah—and among those who transmitted that from him was Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari: Abu Usamah narrated to us, Burayd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "Indeed, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intends mercy for a nation among His servants, He takes its prophet before it, making him a forerunner and pioneer ahead of it. But when He intends the destruction of a nation, He punishes it while its prophet is alive, destroying it while he watches, thereby cooling his eye with its destruction when they disbelieved him and disobeyed his command."
And Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated it to me, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Salim narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, and he said 'beautified it' instead of 'completed it.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Salim ibn Hayyan narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Mina' narrated to us, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "The similitude of me and the similitude of the prophets is like that of a man who built a house and completed and perfected it except for the place of a brick. People began entering it and marveling at it, saying: If only the place of this brick were filled! The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "So I am the place of that brick; I came and concluded the prophets."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The similitude of me and the similitude of the prophets..." and he mentioned the like of it.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The similitude of me and the prophets before me is like that of a man who built a building and made it handsome and beautiful, except for the place of a brick in one of its corners. People began circumambulating it and marveling at it, saying: If only this brick were placed! He said: So I am that brick, and I am the seal of the prophets."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, he said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which: And Abu al-Qasim (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The similitude of me and the prophets before me is like that of a man who built houses, making them handsome, beautiful, and complete, except for the place of a brick in one of their corners. People began circumambulating them and admiring the building, saying: Why didn't you place a brick here so your building would be complete? Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "So I was that brick."

'Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "The similitude of me and the prophets is like that of a man who built a building, making it handsome and beautiful. People began circling around it, saying: We have never seen a building more handsome than this, except for this missing brick! So I was that brick."

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Salim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Mina', from Jabir, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The similitude of me and you is like that of a man who lit a fire, and grasshoppers and moths began falling into it while he was trying to drive them away from it; and I am holding onto your waistbands to keep you from the Fire, while you are slipping away from my hands."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, he said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "My similitude is like that of a man who lit a fire, and when it illuminated what was around it, moths and these insects that fall into fire began dropping into it, while he was holding them back, but they overpowered him and rushed headlong into it." He said: "So that is the similitude of me and you: I am holding onto your waistbands to keep you from the Fire, saying: Come away from the Fire! Come away from the Fire! Yet you overpower me and rush headlong into it."
And 'Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated it to us, they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, with this chain of transmission, similar to it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Qurashi narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The similitude of me and the similitude of my community is only like that of a man who kindled a fire, and insects and moths began falling into it; so I am holding onto your waistbands while you are plunging into it."

'Abdullah ibn Barrad al-Ash'ari and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Kurayb's—they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "Indeed, the similitude of me and that with which Allah has sent me is like that of a man who came to his people and said: O my people, I have seen the army with my own eyes, and I am the naked warner, so flee, flee! A group of his people obeyed him and departed in the early night, moving off safely at an unhurried pace. But another group of them called him a liar and remained in their places until morning; the army attacked them at dawn, destroying them and wiping them out. That is the similitude of whoever obeys me and follows what I have brought, and the similitude of whoever disobeys me and rejects what I have brought of the truth."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu 'Amir al-Ash'ari, and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us—and the wording is Abu 'Amir's—they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "The similitude of the guidance and knowledge with which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sent me is like that of abundant rain that falls upon land. Part of it is good soil that accepts the water and brings forth plenty of herbage and grass. Another part of it is barren ground that holds the water, and Allah benefits people through it so that they drink from it, irrigate with it, and graze their animals. And it falls upon another part of it which is only flat rock; it holds no water and brings forth no herbage. That is the similitude of one who gains understanding in the religion of Allah and benefits from that with which Allah has sent me, so he learns and teaches; and the similitude of one who pays no regard to it and does not accept the guidance of Allah with which I was sent."

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us, Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that a man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asking him for food, so he gave him half a wasq of barley. The man, his wife, and their guest continued eating from it until he weighed it. He then went to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Had you not measured it, you would have eaten from it and it would have remained for you."

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us, Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that Umm Malik used to gift clarified butter to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in a small leather skin of hers. Her sons would come to her asking for condiment when they had nothing, so she would go to the container in which she used to gift to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and find butter in it. It continued to provide the condiment of her household until she squeezed it. She went to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and he said: "Did you squeeze it?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Had you left it, it would have continually remained."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was at al-Zawra' when a vessel of water was brought to him which did not submerge his fingers, or barely covered his fingers; then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Hisham.

Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i narrated to me, Mu'adh—meaning Ibn Hisham—narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and his Companions were at al-Zawra'—he said: and al-Zawra' is in Medina near the market and the mosque, around there—he called for a cup containing water and placed his palm in it, and water began gushing out from between his fingers, so all of his Companions performed ablution. He said: I asked: "How many were they, O Abu Hamzah?" He said: "They were approximately three hundred."

Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to me, Ma'n narrated to us, Malik narrated to us; (H) and Abu al-Tahir narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, that he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) when the time for the 'Asr prayer had arrived. The people searched for ablution water but could not find any. Then ablution water was brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) placed his hand in that vessel and commanded the people to perform ablution from it. He said: I saw the water gushing from beneath his fingers, and the people performed ablution until the very last of them had performed ablution.

Abu al-Rabi', Sulayman ibn Dawud al-'Ataki narrated to me, Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called for water, and a shallow cup was brought to him. The people began performing ablution, and I estimated them to be between sixty and eighty. He said: I kept looking at the water gushing from between his fingers.

Al-Hakam ibn Musa Abu Salih narrated to me, Hiql—meaning Ibn Ziyad—narrated to us, from al-Awza'i: Abu 'Ammar narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Farrukh narrated to me, Abu Hurayrah narrated to me, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I am the leader of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, the first for whom the grave will split open, the first intercessor, and the first whose intercession will be accepted."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman: Simak ibn Harb narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Samurah, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, I know a stone in Mecca that used to greet me with peace before I was sent; indeed, I know it right now."

Muhammad ibn Mihran al-Razi and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahm narrated to us, both from al-Walid—Ibn Mihran said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us—al-Awza'i narrated to us, from Abu 'Ammar, Shaddad, that he heard Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Indeed, Allah chose Kinanah from the offspring of Isma'il, and He chose Quraysh from Kinanah, and He chose Banu Hashim from Quraysh, and He chose me from Banu Hashim."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, from Samurah ibn Jundab, he said: Whenever the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) prayed the morning prayer (Fajr), he would turn his face toward them and say: "Did any of you see a dream last night?"

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, he said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "While I was asleep, the treasures of the earth were brought to me, and two gold bracelets were placed in my hands. They weighed heavily upon me and distressed me, but it was inspired to me to blow on them. So I blew on them and they vanished. I interpreted them as the two liars between whom I am located: the ruler of Sanaa and the ruler of al-Yamamah."

Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Tamimi narrated to me, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Husayn: Nafi' ibn Jubayr narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: Musaylimah the Liar came to Medina during the lifetime of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), saying: "If Muhammad gives me authority after him, I will follow him." He came with a large number of his people. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) approached him, accompanied by Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and in the hand of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was a piece of a palm stalk. When he stood before Musaylimah among his companions, he said: "If you were to ask me for this piece of palm stalk, I would not give it to you. I will never transgress the command of Allah concerning you, and if you turn back, Allah will surely destroy you. Indeed, I perceive that you are the one shown to me in the vision I was shown, and here is Thabit who will answer you on my behalf." Then he turned away from him. Ibn 'Abbas said: I asked about the saying of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Indeed, I perceive that you are the one shown to me in the vision I was shown," and Abu Hurayrah informed me that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "While I was asleep, I saw two gold bracelets on my hands, and their presence distressed me. It was inspired to me in the dream to blow upon them, so I blew upon them and they flew away. I interpreted them as two liars who would arise after me; one of them was al-'Ansi, the ruler of Sanaa, and the other was Musaylimah, the ruler of al-Yamamah."

Abu 'Amir, 'Abdullah ibn Barrad al-Ash'ari, and Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us—and their wordings were close—they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, his grandfather, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "I saw in a dream that I was emigrating from Mecca to a land with date palms. My initial thought went to it being al-Yamamah or Hajar, but behold, it was the city of Medina (Yathrib). And I saw in this dream of mine that I brandished a sword and its tip broke; and behold, that represented what befell the believers on the day of Uhud. Then I brandished it another time, and it returned to the best condition it had ever been; and behold, that represented the victory that Allah brought and the uniting of the believers. And I also saw in it cows—and what is with Allah is good—and behold, they were the group of believers martyred on the day of Uhud; and the good was that which Allah brought afterwards of good, and the reward of sincerity which Allah granted us after the day of Badr."
